---
title: Quick start
description: Read a verified price, then put it on CKB testnet in your own feed cell.
---

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install

```bash
npm install lean-oracle-sdk @ckb-ccc/core
```

The SDK runs in Node 20+ and in browsers. `@ckb-ccc/core` is only needed for the parts that talk to
CKB.

</Step>
<Step>

### Read a verified price

```ts
import { LeanOracleTestnetClient } from "lean-oracle-sdk/client";

const oracle = new LeanOracleTestnetClient();
const [btc] = await oracle.latestPrices(["Crypto.BTC/USDT"], "majors");

// Prices are integers with an exponent: value = price × 10^expo.
console.log(Number(btc.price) * 10 ** btc.expo, new Date(Number(btc.publishTimeMs)));
```

The client fetches the latest update from the public mirror and checks the committee's signatures
against the committee cell on chain before returning. It never trusts the mirror's JSON. Feed names
and IDs are listed in [Price feeds](/docs/feeds).

</Step>
<Step>

### Create your feed cell

Contracts read prices from a feed cell that you own. Create one once, with a funded testnet key (get
testnet CKB from the [faucet](https://faucet.nervos.org)). A feed cell locks about 280 CKB, which you
get back if you burn it.

```ts
import { ccc } from "@ckb-ccc/core";

const signer = new ccc.SignerCkbPrivateKey(oracle.cccClient, process.env.PRIVATE_KEY!);

async function send(tx: ccc.Transaction) {
  const fee = await oracle.completeFee(tx, signer);
  if (fee.status === "insufficient") throw new Error(`Needs ${fee.shortfall} more shannons`);
  return signer.sendTransaction(fee.tx);
}

const { tx, typeScript } = await oracle.createFeedCell({ signer, feed: "Crypto.BTC/USDT", committee: "majors" });
await send(tx);
// Save typeScript: it identifies your feed cell from now on.
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Move it to the latest price

```ts
const update = await oracle.pullAndUpdate(typeScript);
await send(update.tx);
console.log(update.after.price, update.after.publishTimeMs);
```

`pullAndUpdate` fetches the latest signed update, verifies it and builds the transaction. Run it
whenever your application needs a fresh price, usually in the same transaction that uses the price.

</Step>
<Step>

### Read it in your contract

Your contract takes the feed cell as a cell dep and checks it with
[`lean-oracle-common`](/docs/reference/rust). The [tutorial](/docs/build/tutorial) walks through a
complete contract.

</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="warn" title="Before you ship">
  Read [Your responsibilities](/docs/build/responsibilities). The oracle proves a price is authentic;
  your contract must decide whether it is fresh enough.
</Callout>
